content:
Over the past year, we've been anticipating the next-generation iPad mini refresh, and it sounds like the announcement is just around the corner. Aaron Perris revealed last week that the new product will feature an A20 Pro chip and narrower screen bezels, and we already know it will sport an OLED display with a water-resistant design.

While these upgrades are already impressive, my primary expectation for the next iPad mini comes down to software.

Having seen iPhone Duo, I'm blown away by Apple's multitasking capabilities. The multitasking experience on iPad has always felt cluttered to me, whereas iPhone Duo feels elegant and smooth.

On such a small screen, traditional windowed operations have never really suited the iPad mini. Users probably won't be stacking many windows on it either. That's why I hope Apple can borrow a practical feature from iPhone Duo: split view combined with picture-in-picture.

What I mean is, it's truly a fantastic experience. Currently on iPad mini, you can't make a picture-in-picture window occupy the full width of the screen in portrait mode; even if you could, it would either obscure part of the app content or require manual resizing through window controls.

Bringing split video and app viewing to the iPad mini's screen seems like a no-brainer to me, especially considering that iPhone Duo and the iPad mini have similar screen aspect ratios. At least for me personally, if this feature were available, I'd use the iPad mini in portrait mode far more often.
